chunks.label: Got it or not
chunks.rationale: Tell someone you understood, or that you didn't.
chunks.interference: wakarimashita and wakarimasen differ only in the ending, so listen for -shita versus -sen.

chunks.label: When you didn't catch it
chunks.rationale: Get people to repeat or slow down, and handle the compliment learners always get.
chunks.interference: kikoenakatta is about hearing; wakarimasen is about understanding.
members: もう一度お願いします
ゆっくり話してください

chunks.label: Agreeing strongly
chunks.rationale: Say 'yes, exactly' and 'I know the feeling', with friends or to a boss.
chunks.interference: wakaru wakaru means 'I feel the same', not 'I understand'.

chunks.label: Tired or fine
chunks.rationale: Say how you feel and how you slept.
chunks.interference: yoku neta uses neru (sleep); nemurenakatta uses nemureru (can sleep).

chunks.label: Hungry, thirsty, full
chunks.rationale: Say you're hungry, thirsty, full or drunk.
chunks.interference: hara hetta is rough; onaka pekopeko works for anyone.

chunks.label: How was it
chunks.rationale: Ask how something went and say it was fun or good.
chunks.interference: tanoshikatta is for fun you had; omoshirokatta is for something interesting or funny.

chunks.label: Giving your opinion
chunks.rationale: Ask what someone thinks, then agree or hedge.
chunks.interference: A drawn-out uun is 'hmm', but a quick dropping uun means no.

chunks.label: Shouts and exclamations
chunks.rationale: Recognize the quick outbursts of surprise, scolding and frustration.
chunks.interference: kora scolds; it isn't a general 'hey'.

chunks.label: What do you mean
chunks.rationale: Ask for an explanation or what someone is getting at.
chunks.interference: nan no hanashi and nan no koto are near twins; dou iu koto asks for the reason.

chunks.label: Correcting a mix-up
chunks.rationale: Say 'no, that's not it' and push back on a plan.
chunks.interference: sou ja nakute corrects what was meant; sou wa ikanai refuses an easy way out.

chunks.label: Getting attention
chunks.rationale: Get someone's attention before you speak, and respond when they show you something.
chunks.interference: ano alone is just 'um'; ooi calls to someone far away.

chunks.label: Things you just learned
chunks.rationale: React to news, or to something you missed.
chunks.interference: shiranakatta is for facts; kizukanakatta is for things you failed to see.

chunks.label: Emergencies and getting help
chunks.rationale: Call for help or an ambulance, warn of an earthquake, and show where it hurts.
chunks.interference: tasukete is for danger; tetsudatte is help with a task.

chunks.label: Lost and getting around
chunks.rationale: Say you're lost and ask the way.
chunks.interference: None.
members: どう行けばいいですか

chunks.label: Broken or lost things
chunks.rationale: Report that something broke, won't work, or went missing.
chunks.interference: nakushita is lost for good; wasuremono shita is left somewhere.

chunks.label: Mistakes and running late
chunks.rationale: Own up to a slip or say you'll be late.
chunks.interference: machigaechatta is your own mistake; machigatteru says something is wrong.

chunks.label: At your limit
chunks.rationale: Say you can't take any more.
chunks.interference: mou dame, mou muri and mou genkai overlap; mou muri is the most casual.

chunks.label: Nerves and relief
chunks.rationale: Say you're nervous, then relieved or feeling better.
chunks.interference: anshin shita and hotto shita are near twins; kinchou isn't excitement.

chunks.label: That's how it goes
chunks.rationale: Concede a point or accept how things are.
chunks.interference: All start with sou or sore; sorya sou da is 'obviously', sore wa sou is 'fair point'.

chunks.label: Kidding and asides
chunks.rationale: Mark what you say as a joke, a warning, a secret or a long story.
chunks.interference: None.

chunks.label: Steering the conversation
chunks.rationale: Wrap up a plan, pick up a story, or change the topic.
chunks.interference: sou iu koto de wraps things up; sou iu koto ka is 'oh, I see'.
members: じゃあ、そういうことで

chunks.label: Feeling refreshed
chunks.rationale: Say a bath, a drink or a clean-up made you feel better.
chunks.interference: sukkiri is cleared up inside; sappari is clean and fresh.

drops.reason: Duplicates 緊張する; the phrase entry covers it.
